paper.title: Optimal discovery with probabilistic expert advice: finite time analysis and macroscopic optimality

settings.name_in_paper: Optimal discovery with probabilistic expert advice (non-intersecting supports, assumption (i))
unmapped: Each expert i draws i.i.d. items from an arbitrary distribution P_i on a countable set; reward is 1 only when a not-yet-discovered interesting item (in A) is observed, so the reward probability (missing mass) decreases with the number of pulls of that expert (state-dependent, rested rotting).
Assumption (i): interesting items of different experts have non-intersecting supports.
Learner observes whether the drawn item is interesting and which item it is.
Regret is measured against an oracle policy (OCL greedy on true missing mass, or omniscient oracle for waiting time).
settings.definition_quote: at each time step $t\in\N^*$, one picks an index $I_t\in\{1,\dots, K\}$, and one observes $X_{I_t, n_{I_t,t}}$ ... The goal is to choose the $(I_t)_{t\geq 1}$ so as to observe as many elements of $A$ as possible in a fixed horizon $t$ ... (i) non-intersecting supports: $A \cap \supp(P_i) \cap \supp(P_j) = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$.

settings.name_in_paper: Macroscopic limit (assumptions (i), (ii), (iii): uniform experts on disjoint supports of size N)
unmapped: Discovery problem: reward is discovering a new interesting item; missing mass decreases with pulls of an expert.
Expert i samples uniformly from its own disjoint support of size N; Q_i^N interesting items with Q_i^N/N -> q_i in (0,1); limit N -> infinity (macroscopic limit).
Performance measured by normalized waiting time T^N(lambda)/N until each expert has at most N*lambda undiscovered interesting items.
settings.definition_quote: (ii) finite supports with the same cardinality: $|\supp(P_i)| = N$ ... (iii) uniform distributions: $P_i(x) = \frac{1}{N}$ ... The macroscopic limit that we investigate in this section corresponds to the setting where $N$ goes to infinity together with the $Q^N_i$ in such a way that $Q^N_i/N \to q_i\in (0,1)$.

conditions: assumption (i): non-intersecting supports of interesting items across experts

source.label: th:firstBound
source.quote: For any $t \geq 1$, under assumption (i), Good-UCB (with constant $C=(1+\sqrt{2})\sqrt{3}$) satisfies \[\E\left[F^*(t)-F^{UCB}(t)\right] \leq 17 \sqrt{K t \log(t)}  + 20\sqrt{K t} + K+ K\log(t/K) \;.\]

results.notes: Quantity is E[F*(t) - F^UCB(t)], difference in number of interesting items found versus the OCL oracle policy (optimal in expectation by Lemma 1); paper's t is T. Recorded as 'other' since it is not standard regret against a fixed arm. Algorithm's index uses log(4t), no horizon needed.

bound.expression_latex: T_{UCB}(\lambda) \leq T^* + K S \log \left(8 T^* + 16 K S \log( K S ) \right), T^* = T^*\left(\lambda - \frac{3}{S} - 2  (1+\sqrt{2}) \sqrt{\frac{c+2}{S}} \right)

symbols.S_c: free analysis parameter S >= 1 of the theorem (not a norm bound)
symbols.c_alg: constant c > 0 in the confidence parameter
symbols.T_star_lam: waiting time of the omniscient oracle at level lambda_w - 3/S_c - 2*(1+sqrt(2))*sqrt((c_alg+2)/S_c)

conditions: holds simultaneously for all lambda in (0,1) with probability at least 1 - K/(c*S^c)

source.label: th:nlregret
source.quote: Let $c > 0$ and $S \geq 1$. Under assumption (i), Good-UCB (with constant $C=(1+\sqrt{2})\sqrt{c+2}$) satisfies with probability at least $1 - \frac{K}{c S^{c}}$, for any $\lambda \in (0,1)$, T_{UCB}(\lambda) \leq T^* + K S \log \left(8 T^* + 16 K S \log( K S ) \right), where T^* = T^*\left(\lambda - \frac{3}{S} - 2  (1+\sqrt{2}) \sqrt{\frac{c+2}{S}} \right)

results.notes: Bound on waiting time T_UCB(lambda) of Good-UCB relative to the omniscient oracle's waiting time at a slightly smaller level; 'non-linear regret'. Quantity 'other'.

symbols.N_sz: support size N of each expert (limit N -> infinity)
symbols.q_i: limiting proportion of interesting items on expert i
symbols.lambda_w: limiting target level lambda (normalized undiscovered interesting items per expert)

source.quote: Take $C=(1+\sqrt{2})\sqrt{c+2}$ with $c>3/2$ in Algorithm~\ref{algo:GUCB}. Under assumption (i), (ii) and (iii), for every sequence $(\lambda^N)_N$ converging to $\lambda$ as $N$ goes to infinity, almost surely \[\limsup_{N \to +\infty} \frac{T_{UCB}^N(\lambda^N)}{N} \leq \sum_{i: q_i>\lambda} \log\frac{q_i}{\lambda}\;.\]

results.notes: Normalized waiting time bound (macroscopic optimality); expression multiplied by N to express waiting time, limsup of T/N <= sum. Matches the OCL limit of Theorem 3.

bound.regime: macroscopic limit N -> infinity, lambda in (0, q_1)

symbols.N_sz: support size N of each expert
symbols.q_i: limiting proportion of interesting items on expert i

source.label: th:OCL
source.quote: For every $\lambda\in (0, q_1)$, for every sequence $(\lambda^N)_N$ converging to $\lambda$ as $N$ goes to infinity, under assumption (i), (ii) and (iii), almost surely \[\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{T_{OCL}^N(\lambda^N)}{N} = \sum_{i: q_i>\lambda} \log\frac{q_i}{\lambda}  \;.\]

results.notes: Exact almost-sure limit of the normalized waiting time of the oracle OCL policy (which knows the true missing masses); not a learning algorithm. Recorded as 'exact' limit, expression scaled by N.

bound.regime: macroscopic limit N -> infinity, lambda in (0, q_1)

symbols.N_sz: support size N of each expert
symbols.q_1: largest limiting proportion of interesting items among experts

source.label: prop:unif
source.quote: For every $\lambda\in (0, q_1)$, for every sequence $(\lambda^N)_N$ converging to $\lambda$ as $N$ goes to infinity, under assumption (i), (ii) and (iii), almost surely \[\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{T_{US}^N(\lambda^N)}{N} = K \log\frac{q_1}{\lambda}\;.\]

results.notes: Exact limit for uniform round-robin sampling; shows macroscopic suboptimality. Proof omitted in paper.
